comments.author: @tysoncung
comments.text: The thing that stuck with me: the world record dew point of 35C was set at Dhahran on 8 July 2003 while the air was only 42C. Far from a record temperature, but at that humidity sweat stops working and the body cannot shed heat. The Gulf does it because it is shallow, almost closed, and loses 1.8m a year to evaporation while getting back 8cm of rain. Sources are in the description. Which have you actually found harder to be outside in, dry desert heat or sticky coastal heat?
